# Film Development Settings: The General Tab

The **General** tab (**Settings** > **Organization** > **Film Development** > **General**) holds the workflow switch, your stages, and the settings that decide how film jobs finish themselves. This article walks it top to bottom.

---

## Workflow mode

The choice at the top decides how film scans are handled:

*   **Film Scans** — the classic workflow: uploaded rolls appear in the Film Scans page for manual association.
*   **Film Development** — the full workflow this section of the Knowledge Base covers: the legacy Film Scans page is hidden, and roll folders are auto-matched to jobs by their twin-check code.

Switching to Film Development doesn't delete anything — the legacy page is hidden, not erased, and you can switch back.

![Film Development Selected](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/ac9104fc-40f1-4027-baa5-ccaa4c272933.png)

---

## Stages

Choose which stages your lab runs. Twin checking isn't listed — it's where each roll gets its identity, so it's always on. With every stage below turned off, your lab runs twin checking only, and scan uploads carry on arriving through the OrderHub Downloader as before.

*   **Receive (order book-in)** — book a mail-in order in and count the rolls against what the customer ordered, before twin checking. Turn off if your team starts at twin checking.
*   **Develop** — rolls queue for developing. Turn off and rolls skip straight past it; past develop history is kept.
*   **Scan** — rolls queue for scanning. Turn off and rolls skip straight past it; past scan history is kept.

Each stage row also carries its own **Send notifications** settings — switch these on to message the customer as their order clears that stage, with your own email and text wording.

Turning a stage off never loses history: switch it back on later and everything is as it was.

### Only expecting film that's in transit

Most labs don't want to book in film handed over at the counter — it's already in your hands. You can limit the Receive list to orders that are actually on their way, using order tags:

1. **Tag the orders as they arrive.** In your website configuration, open the **Filters** tab and add a rule for each delivery route — for example, when the order's custom field `film_delivery` equals `mail-in`, tag the order **mail-in**. Add another rule for drop-box orders if you use them. Your storefront just needs to send the field; the rule does the tagging.
2. **Tell Film Development which tags to expect.** Under the **Receive** row here on the General tab, enter those tags (for example *mail-in*, *drop-box*).

![Receive Row - Expected Tags](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/7404c8db-338a-4abb-a5c3-517a76e0d9ec.png)

From then on, only orders carrying one of those tags appear in the expected list and count as "orders expected" in the Film Development App. Film handed over in store never appears — and if a customer posts film in without choosing the right option at checkout, staff can still book any order in by scanning its number. Booked-in orders get your "received safely" notification (if switched on) whichever way they arrived.

---

## Email

The **Open email settings** button opens your per-brand film-scan email content: subject, body, from name, reply-to, BCC, logo, gallery URL prefix and direct-download domain, plus the Film Development email trigger mode (**Per job** / **Per order** / **Manual**). If your organization has multiple websites, pick the brand inside the dialog.

---

## Auto-complete film jobs when all rolls are uploaded

With this on, each film job completes itself once every roll's scans have arrived — and for develop-only work, once developing is done. The order then completes only when every job on it (including any print jobs created from the scans) is finished. You'll see the completion recorded in the job's activity, so it's always clear why a job closed.

With it off, film jobs wait to be completed by hand.

---

## When every roll on a job ends with an exception

Sometimes every roll on a job ends with an exception — blank, damaged, can't be processed. This choice decides what happens to the job:

| Choice | What it means |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Leave the job open** | The default — nothing happens automatically; you deal with the job by hand. |
| **Complete the job** | The work counts as done — the developing was attempted and the customer is charged as normal. |
| **Cancel the job** | The work counts as never happened — useful where your policy is to refund. |

Completing and cancelling can affect pricing and invoicing differently, so this is deliberately your call. The change is recorded in the job's activity as *"All rolls ended by exception"*.

![Film Completion Settings](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/333d7c70-a343-4403-8ba8-ad28c45389c5.png)

---

## Auto-complete Pick-Up orders when film delivered

Only closes pure-film pickup orders once the customer's scans are delivered by email — so a pickup order whose only contents are film doesn't sit open waiting for a collection that already happened digitally.

---

## Auto-release scan-attached artwork

When a film scan is attached to an automatically created print job, this marks the artwork production-ready and releases the job to production automatically. Turn it off if operators need to review scans before OrderHub Desktop picks them up.

---

## Good to know

*   These settings only take effect in **Film Development** workflow mode — in Film Scans mode the classic behaviour applies throughout.
*   The completion settings are off by default and never act on history: switching one on affects work from that moment forward, not jobs already sitting open.
